narrative_markdown:
## Today's Forecast

A high of 26°C (79°F) is expected with afternoon showers and thunderstorms developing from 16:00, bringing 11.9 mm (0.47 in) of rain. Thunder possible from the morning, peaking this evening. Skies will be mostly cloudy through early and midday hours, turning overcast by evening. Winds start from the northeast early, with no agreed bearing by midday or evening, reaching peak gusts of 33 km/h (18 kt) ashore. The UV index will peak at 8.3. Air quality measured at Kisumu Airport shows an AQI of 3. Overnight, temperatures will drop to a low of 18°C (64°F) forecast calls for 100% rain probability night and day combined. As of 06:01, reports through 04:00: no rain; no thunder; high so far 19°C (66°F); low so far 18°C (64°F); peak sustained 7 km/h (4 kt); sky partly cloudy.

## Extended Outlook

Temperatures and winds much the same through Monday, with rain and thunderstorms possible Saturday, and rain and thunderstorms likely from Sunday. Skies mostly cloudy throughout. Monday's call: rain, 94%, with all four models wet; highs around 27°C (80°F). Kenya Meteorological Department (KMD) calls it dry. At this lead ECMWF has the best record, right 90% of the time over 90 checks.

Further out, temperatures and winds much the same through Friday, with showers and thunderstorms likely Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday, and showers and thunderstorms possible Friday. Tuesday: all four models wet, highs around 27°C (81°F). Wednesday: all four models wet, highs around 28°C (82°F). Thursday: all three models that reach it wet, highs around 28°C (83°F).

Only GFS, ECMWF and ICON reach past Wednesday. GFS and ICON are the wetter solutions from Tuesday to Wednesday; ECMWF and UKMO keep it drier. Friday's call: rain, 100%, with both models wet; highs around 29°C (83°F). At this lead ECMWF has the best record, right 93% of the time over 86 checks.

## Severe Weather / Hazard Potential

Convective instability in the hours ahead: UKMO 2430 J/kg, ECMWF 1790 J/kg, GFS 520 J/kg and ICON 490 J/kg. Thunder possible; any thunderstorm brings sudden gusts well above the 33 km/h (18 kt) forecast.

## Winam Gulf — Conditions for Boaters

Peak gust 23 km/h (13 kt). Any thunderstorm brings sudden gusts well above this figure; the water is unsafe while one is nearby.

## Detailed Discussion

### Synoptic Overview

Across roughly 2,600 km, pressure is lowest toward the north (1013 hPa) and highest toward the northeast (1017 hPa) — a 4 hPa spread, a weak large-scale gradient. The lower pressure to the north is deepening over the next three days. Pressure is also falling toward the west — a large-scale feature building in that direction, though this sampling cannot say how fast or whether it will reach here. Pressure overhead is falling. Sampling is a nine-point ring at 12-degree spacing, so this locates a direction, not a centre or a front. Across the basin's 5 points, pressure today sits between 1017.4 and 1019.4 hPa, falling by 1.7 hPa over three days. Pressure here over the last 24 hours: -0.2 hPa.

### Forecaster Confidence Notes

On rain the record ranks ECMWF first at Day+3, right 90% of the last 30 checks and ECMWF first at Day+7, right 93% of the last 30 checks. On today's high UKMO is the warmest model at 27.2°C (81.0°F) and ICON the coolest at 23.7°C (74.7°F); the call's 25.8°C (78.4°F) sits between them. At Day+0, no model is meaningfully better than the others here yet. At Day+3, ECMWF is the strongest rain caller here and kenya_met the weakest. At Day+7, ECMWF is the strongest rain caller here and GFS the weakest.
